minutes.headline: Commission halted a volunteer's mountain-bike trail grooming until he submits a mapped plan and gets permission
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission continued four wetlands hearings (Mopus Road, Summer Street, Northfield Road culvert, Fire Road 15A) to January 7 for more information. It also told a volunteer to stop grooming trails until he submits a map, approved a permit extension for Shirley Reservoir Road, and handled Hollis Road property expenses.

public_comment.topic: Praised the volunteer trail grooming and maintenance work at Lunenburg Town Forest.

budget_items.topic: Consultant review fee cap in the bylaw
budget_items.what_was_said: The bylaw caps the consultant fee at a low amount for project costs up to a set threshold. The commission discussed moving the cap into an easier-to-change regulation.
A member proposed budgeting for the annual heating service, asking for a not-to-exceed approval.
The chair listed bills already paid for locks, electric turn-on, and oil delivery, to be approved after the fact from the Hollis fund.

budget_items.topic: Marcel monitoring device for Hollis Road
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission discussed buying a remote temperature monitor for the vacant building, noting a sale price and a monthly subscription fee.

budget_items.topic: Zero Shirley Reservoir Road permit extension
budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant requested extending the order of conditions ahead of the project going to bid.

decisions.decision: Trail grooming is halted until the volunteer submits a marked-up map of trails and gets commission approval.
Applicants left off the agenda due to a posting error will be rescheduled to January 7, 2026.
The conservation agent will be asked to issue an emergency certification for a hazardous tree at 98 Horizon Island Road.
The bylaw's consultant fee cap should be revisited via an easier-to-change regulation.
The future use of the Hollis Road residence will be a full future agenda item.

what_happened.line: The Commission halted a volunteer's mountain-bike trail grooming at the Town Forest until he submits a mapped trail plan and gets its approval.
Four wetlands hearings -- Mopus Road, Summer Street, a Northfield Road culvert, and Fire Road 15A -- were continued to January 7 for more information.
The Commission voted to cover Hollis Road property costs from the Hollis fund, including a heating-service contract, back bills, and a remote monitoring device for the vacant building.
The order of conditions for Zero Shirley Reservoir Road was extended to August 2029 ahead of the project going to bid.
Members discussed moving the bylaw's consultant-fee cap into an easier-to-change regulation rather than the bylaw itself.

why_it_matters: Anyone using the Town Forest's mountain-bike trails will see grooming paused until a plan is on file, a condition tied to volunteer maintenance work residents praised in public comment.
The four continued hearings mean the property owners at those addresses face another wait before any wetlands permit is decided.
The town-owned Hollis Road property is now drawing recurring costs from its dedicated fund, and its longer-term use is set to come back as a full agenda item.
watch_next: The continued hearings for 480 Mopus Road, 30 Summer Street, the Northfield Road culvert, and 27 Fire Road 15A resume January 7, 2026.
A future agenda item on the long-term use of the Hollis Road residence.
